en:
...Hello, everyone. Nice to meet you.
My name is Shoji Arai, from Class 2-B.
This may surprise you all, but I was in the soccer club, you know.
Back in my first year.
I quit after a year, though.
I suppose it just wasn't for me.
The practices were hard, and even to be generous, my athletic ability was nothing to speak of.
But you see, the real reason was something else.
Did you know this school has a fully equipped lodge?
Surprisingly few people know about it.
There's the auditorium, isn't there?
The auditorium where they hold graduation and other ceremonies.
Have you ever been up above that auditorium?
I don't suppose you have.
It's normally off-limits.
And hardly anyone ever uses it.
Apparently plenty of people spend three years at this school and graduate without ever knowing what's up there.
But you see, a certain few know it well.
They know there's a lodge up there.{p}

It can sleep about fifty people.
The athletic clubs use it when a tournament is coming up, or when they hold a training camp at school.
But apparently it's really only a few of the athletic clubs that use it.
And do you know why? ...Things appear in that lodge.
Why would that be, I wonder?
I have no idea why they'd appear in a place like that.
But the rumors about that place don't stop at one or two.{p}
When it comes to scary stories, what kind interests you most?
Ghost stories
Strange stories
Cruel stories
Disgusting stories

...I see.
So you like strange stories.
As it happens, I think the story I'm about to tell is perfect for someone like you.
I think you'll be satisfied.
...Yes.
After all, even I, who actually lived through it, still don't really understand it.
...It happened during summer vacation last year.{p}

You know the soccer club is split into a first team and a second team, don't you?
And the second-team players, which is to say people like us, were made to hold a training camp at school.
Of course, we didn't get the same treatment or standing as the first team's core players, the regulars included.
First-team players don't stay overnight at school.
We hardly ever even got to see them.
However you looked at it, we had neither the talent nor the grit to move up to the first team.
If anything, rather than getting stronger or winning tournaments, I'd have been happy just to have fun in club activities.
But according to the first-team people, that makes you a loser.
The second team is a bunch of losers like that.
Players get dropped from the first team to the second, but almost nobody ever moves up from the second to the first.
But for me, that actually made it easier.
So what if you're a loser, as long as you're having fun?{p}
You think so too, don't you, {a}?
Being a loser is fine by me
I don't want to be a loser
I don't care either way

...I see.
So you're on a different side from me, {a}.{p}

In this world, you see, there are people who rule and people who are ruled.
You're the ruling type, aren't you?
Me, I find it more comfortable being ruled.
...I see.
So that's the kind of person you are, {a}.
...Well, never mind.
Let's go on with the story.{p}

I liked the soccer club, that bunch of losers, because it was easygoing, but some people in it didn't feel that way.
Our soccer club is fairly strong, after all.
It was a far cry from the fun club activities I'd pictured.
The practices were hard, and everyone was serious.
But you see, plenty of people felt the same way I did.
People who wanted a friendlier, more relaxed soccer club, even if it meant being weak.
And so I found a friend I got along with.
A first-year who, like me, hated the harsh practices.{p}

His name was Masaru Sodeyama.
He had a weak constitution.
Apparently his mother told him he had to, so he reluctantly joined an athletic club.
He figured the soccer club had lots of members, so he'd be able to slack off.
Pretty much the same as me, right?
But once he actually joined, it was nothing like that, and he was depressed.
We became friends right away.
By then, we were already the soccer club's washouts.
We could have quit any time.
But Sodeyama was a good guy.
He said his mother would be sad if he quit the soccer club, so he kept at it without missing a single one of those hellish, grueling practices.
Frankly, I wanted to quit, but Sodeyama was there.
So I kept him company and kept at it too.{p}

Besides, they say that if you were in an athletic club as a student, it goes over well in job interviews, don't they?
So I kept at it, too.
And then came the summer training camp.
I don't much like training camps.
Being forced to live a regimented life as a group, controlled twenty-four hours a day.
I think that sort of thing is unforgivable.
And it went on for a whole week.
If Sodeyama hadn't been there, I'd have skipped the camp and just quit the soccer club.
I'm no good at living in a group...
When the camp starts, the first thing they do is show you to the lodge, and you pick your own bed.{p}

My first sight of the lodge left a thoroughly gloomy impression.
As for windows, there were only small skylights you could barely get your head through, if that, and not one bit of sunlight came in.
It was like a prison, damp and clammy, with soulless bunk beds lined up in a grid like a go board.
That was all.
They call it a lodge, but there's nothing but beds.
The beds were metal-pipe frames with no reading lamps, and the mattresses were thin and rock-hard.
It was like sleeping on bare tatami.
Frankly, it felt less like a lodge than an internment camp.
Even so, there were guys who were thrilled about the camp.
Everyone eating together, everyone sleeping together.
Some people's hearts leap at that kind of group life.
Not that I can understand it.
"I got this bed!"
"This one's mine!"
They all shouted things like that, fighting over the beds they wanted.
I'd have thought every bed was the same.
"Arai, where should we go?"
Sodeyama asked me that.
If we could, it'd be better to be next to each other, right?
Sodeyama was the only one there I thought I'd get along with.
When I looked, almost all the beds were already taken.
Even if we wanted to choose, the only spot with two empty beds side by side was...{p}

"...Looks like this is the only spot."
With that, Sodeyama tossed his bag up onto the top bunk of a bed far from the entrance.
The bed to its right was empty.
"Then I'll take this one."
I put my things on the bed to the right of the one Sodeyama had chosen.
"...Hey, that guy picked bed number 4."
"...Yeah.
What an idiot."
I didn't miss the two guys whispering to each other nearby.{p}

Bed number 4?
I looked carefully at the edge of the bed frame.
My bed was marked with the number "2."
Sodeyama didn't seem to have noticed what those two were saying.
When I quietly peeked at his bed...{p}

His bed was marked with the number "4."
That was when I first realized it.
That Sodeyama was drawing a great deal of attention.
Everyone was putting their things away and pretending not to look, yet they kept glancing at Sodeyama, or rather, it seemed to be bed number 4 they were worried about.

I wavered over whether to tell Sodeyama about it.
Should I tell him?
Or else...{p}What do you think I did?
You told him
You didn't tell him

From that day on, the grueling practices began.
But after dinner we had free time, so we could relax.
Everyone had brought handheld video game consoles or portable CD players.
Those who hadn't brought them had manga or novels, or cards and games instead, and everyone passed the time in their own way on their beds.
Sodeyama and I talked about all sorts of things, our studies and our hobbies.
Good times always fly by.{p}

Sodeyama was rubbing his sleepy eyes, and he looked somehow haggard.
"Looks like you didn't sleep very well."
When I said that, he gave a little nod.
"You seemed to be having nightmares..."
"...I don't really remember."
He answered wearily.
That was when I noticed.{p}

That there was a small blue bruise on the back of his right hand.
"Where'd you get that bruise?
Did you bump it on something?"
"...Huh, I don't know.
I don't really remember."
He answered as if I were bothering him.{p}

That night, too, Sodeyama seemed to sleep badly.
The next morning, his color was even worse.{p}

And the bruise on his hand had grown bigger than the day before.
It was a bruise that looked painful just to see, as if something heavy had been pressing on it for a long time, or as if someone had pinched it as hard as they could.{p}

"...Sodeyama.
Are you all right?"
"............Yeah."
"Doesn't the bruise on your hand hurt? It looks worse than yesterday."
"............Yeah."
He said very little.{p}

Days like that went on for a while.
And day by day, Sodeyama's health and color got worse.
He looked as if you couldn't tell whether he was alive or dead.
And along with it, the bruise on his right hand grew bigger too, stamping its mark ever more clearly, a dark, murky black.{p}

And at practice on the last day, he finally collapsed.
"The bed... take me to the bed..."
That was all he kept muttering.
It was hot, after all.
We thought it might be sunstroke, so it was decided to let him rest in bed.
It was summer vacation, so the school nurse wasn't there either.
"Arai, you go with him."
One of the upperclassmen told me that, and I took Sodeyama back.
Not that anyone needed to tell me; I'd meant to volunteer for the job anyway.{p}

At that point, I agonized over whether it was really all right to lay him in bed number 4.
Everyone's distant looks, like they wanted nothing to do with it.
And what those two had said to each other.
I remembered it clearly, you see.{p}{a}, what do you think I did then?
Put him in bed number 4
Put him in a different bed

I meant to do that, too.
Not bed number 4; I thought I'd at least let him sleep in my bed.
...But it was no use.
He didn't want to.
For some reason, he wanted to sleep in bed number 4.{p}

Having no choice, I laid him in bed number 4.
"...Hurry up and get out.
...I'm sleepy."
It was a really cold reception.
He chased me off as if I were in his way.
I left the room, leaving Sodeyama there alone.{p}

That damp lodge where no sunlight came in even in the daytime.
Naturally, the stale air there turns dusty and musty.
I didn't want to stay there long either, if I could help it.
...But little by little, I started to worry.
If anything happened to Sodeyama, I'd be the one held responsible.{p}What would you do?
Go back and check on him
Keep on practicing

I see.
...You really are a cold person, aren't you?
I suppose that's how people on the ruling side are.
You can abandon a friend without a second thought.
You have that kind of face, after all.
But I was different.
Friends are important, you know.{p}I was worried about Sodeyama, so I went back to the room.{p}
...Sodeyama was asleep.
He was lying on the bed with the blanket pulled up over his head, and it was squirming.{p}

...But what I'd taken for a blanket was a living thing.
A nameless, caterpillar-like creature, its whole body wrapped in a pale brown, blanket-like cloth, was lying over Sodeyama.
"Ah!"
I cried out before I could stop myself.
The instant I did, the thing stopped moving.{p}
Then it slowly looked my way.

Below the neck it was wrapped tightly in that blanket-like rag, so I couldn't see its whole body.
Not that I wanted to see it, of course.
It had an indescribably horrible face.
You could almost call it a woman's face, but that thing was definitely not human.
It didn't seem like a ghost or anything of that sort either; it was simply an eerie monster.
It had a hand in its mouth.
Sodeyama's right hand.
A shock, as if time had stopped.
All around me, a silent world without a single sound.
If someone had dropped a needle right then, I think I could have heard even that.
And then, in that silent world, what did I hear but a slurp, slurp, like something sipping, like something sucking.
It was sucking on Sodeyama's arm.
On that dark, murky bruise, its lips pursed, it was sucking away.{p}

Then all of a sudden, it opened its mouth wide.
It was a mouth so huge it looked like it could swallow a human head in one gulp.
...I couldn't run away.
Strangely, I even forgot to run.
Fear had frozen me in place, and tangled up with it was the shock of meeting something unknown; between them, my five senses were stolen from me.
It kept glaring at me, its huge mouth still wide open.{p}I couldn't run away. What do you think I did?
You screamed
You prayed
You spat at it
I don't know
I don't know what came over me myself, but I spat.{p}
Right at that monster.{p}

Then all of a sudden, it let out a shrill shriek like fingernails scraping glass, and began to writhe in agony.
Where my spit had hit it, it sizzled and charred and smoke rose up, as if I'd thrown sulfuric acid on it.
I was stunned.
It melted into the air just like that and vanished.{p}

Whether it died or ran away... that I don't know.
Only once it was gone did I hurriedly grab Sodeyama's arm, which hung limply out from under the covers.

"Sodeyama!"
I pulled as hard as I could.
And then I froze in horror.
Sodeyama wasn't there.{p}

What came out from under the covers was only Sodeyama's right arm.
The rest of Sodeyama, the body that should have been past the base of the shoulder, was gone.
...No, to be precise, that's not quite right.
Stuck to the base of the shoulder was something like a plant bulb.
A small thing, small enough to sit in the palm of your hand.
That was Sodeyama.
Wrinkled, shriveled and hardened, it was all that was left of Sodeyama.
It was almost strange that only his right arm was still normal.
Had all the nourishment been sucked out of Sodeyama's body?
And if I'd found him just a little later, would the nourishment in the last thing remaining, his right arm, have been sucked out too, leaving only a wrinkled lump?{p}

Even if I told anyone what happened to Sodeyama, there was no way they'd believe me.
So I kept quiet.
But even if I kept quiet, the fact remained that Sodeyama had disappeared, and I was the one who'd been with him until the end, so I figured I'd be questioned.
But nothing happened.
The moment it came out that Sodeyama had been sleeping in bed number 4, I was called in by the principal.{p}

Even though it was summer vacation, the principal came all the way to school.
And then,
"You saw nothing.
Nothing happened there.
Is that clear?"
he told me, making very sure I understood.{p}

I don't know how that incident was dealt with.
But I never saw Sodeyama again after that, and he didn't come to school even when the second term started.
And I don't know what became of that shriveled thing that was all that was left of Sodeyama, either.
...That's the direct reason I quit the soccer club.
...By the way, after that, I heard the rumor about bed number 4 secondhand.
Apparently, anyone who uses bed number 4 goes missing.
But whenever someone tries to get rid of that bed, something bad happens, so no one dares lay a hand on it.
Still, what was that monster I saw?
Does the principal know something?
A while later, I read in a certain book that some yokai are weak against human spit.
Maybe that thing was one of them.
But I don't believe it died.
If it were the kind of thing that would disappear that easily, someone would have gotten rid of it long ago.
{a}, the day may come when you have to use the lodge, too.
When it does, check whether bed number 4 is still there.
I'm sure it will be.
But I'm warning you, be very careful.
Don't use bed number 4...
This concludes my story.
Next person, please.{p}

I see.
What a coincidence.
The story I've prepared happens to be about a ghost.
{a}, the truth is...
This is a ghost story, but it's also my confession.
Please, hear it through to the end.
...Well then, let me tell it.
You see, there's something else that appears in that lodge besides ghosts.
I'll tell you what it is.{p}

It's a pencil.
Not just any pencil.
It's called the Reaper Pencil.
The Reaper Pencil apparently appears out of nowhere, and then vanishes again.
In other words, only those who are chosen can use it.
Long ago, there was a boy at this school who loved playing Kokkuri-san.
But his version of Kokkuri-san was called 'Lord Reaper,' and it used a pencil instead of a ten-yen coin.
They say the ten-yen coin you use for Kokkuri-san has to be spent or gotten rid of right away.
But after playing 'Lord Reaper,' he never disposed of the pencil he'd used.
Instead, he made a point of using it again every time he played 'Lord Reaper.'
He seems to have believed that by using the same pencil over and over, more and more of Lord Reaper's power would build up inside it.
He's graduated from this school now, but...
One day, he dropped the pencil he'd used for 'Lord Reaper' somewhere and lost it.
Where do you think he dropped it?{p}

...That's right, inside the lodge.
Believe it or not, he'd been in the soccer club, the same as me.
Well, he'd already graduated by the time I joined, so I never met him.
Anyway, about this Reaper Pencil.
They say that if you use it, you can do automatic writing.
The pencil's power moves your hand on its own, and it writes out a certain message.
Now, about that message.
Apparently it reveals the very thing that will get the person using the Reaper Pencil killed.
For example, 'running out into the road,' or 'getting into a fight with someone'...
They say it's a pencil that can predict that kind of thing.
What I'm going to tell you is something that happened involving this Reaper Pencil.
It was last summer.
During the soccer club's training camp, a boy found the Reaper Pencil.
His name was Michio Yamamoto.{p}

On the second night of camp, in the middle of the night, Yamamoto woke up and found a pencil lying by his pillow.
He thought it was school property, so he went to put it somewhere else, and...
The instant he picked it up, it started to move, and his hand, as if guided, began scrawling across the cover of the paperback he'd left beside his bed.
This is what it wrote.

"Going out with the first girl you meet today..."
Moonlight shone in through the window, lighting up the words.
He was stunned.
He didn't know about the Reaper Pencil, so he thought this might be some kind of prophecy.{p}

Once the pencil had finished writing its prophecy of death, it vanished into thin air.
Yamamoto grew restless.
Who would the first girl he met today be?
What kind of girl would she be?
He hoped she'd be cute.
Since they were at camp, maybe it would be one of the girl managers.
Those were the things he thought about.
Everyone around him was asleep.
Yamamoto got up and started getting ready.
He set the newest of the workout clothes he'd brought beside his pillow.
So he could put them on the moment he woke up in the morning.
I woke up to the sound of him rustling around.
And when I looked, there was Yamamoto, gazing at the paperback cover and grinning to himself.{p}

I sensed something strange in the air, so I pretended to be asleep and watched him for a while.
And then...
He looked under the bed and suddenly cried out.
"Whoa!☆"
Wondering what was going on, I strained my eyes, and...{p}

Under his bed, of all things, there was a girl.
"W-who are you?"
Yamamoto was startled, and his face went red.
Then the girl said this.
"I ran away from home..."
The girl was wearing this school's uniform.
She said that she'd run away from home and had come here meaning to stay in the school's lodge.
And so Yamamoto got a bed ready for her, and she slept in the lodge.{p}

The next day, I talked to Yamamoto.
That's how I learned he'd used the Reaper Pencil.
I was shocked.
Of course, I told him right away.
That his automatic writing was the work of the Reaper Pencil's power.
That the Reaper Pencil's prophecies are messages of death.
But he wouldn't listen to what I said.
And he told me not to tell anyone about her.
Yamamoto hid her.
If everyone found her, they'd surely tell her to go home...
That must have been what he thought.{p}

"Even going to school, it's the same thing every day.
Sit through class, go home, go to school again...
Sometimes the teachers scold me, sometimes they praise me.
Day after day of worrying about tests and grades, underlining things in books and notebooks.
I wanted to do something different, so I left home.
I wanted to have some fun experiences over summer vacation..."
What she was saying might have been nothing but selfishness.
But he didn't think so.
She wasn't just thoughtlessly trying to have fun.
She was trying to do something she could only do now.
That's what he thought.
And he decided he would help her with this adventure of hers.
Maybe it had been love at first sight for him.{p}

"That was a prophecy from the Reaper Pencil..."
He couldn't have forgotten what I'd told him.
But he wasn't actually going out with the girl at that point.
So there should be no danger.
That seems to be what he thought.
But then came the fourth day of camp.{p}

"I should be going home soon.
Thanks for everything."
She said this one night when the moonlight was beautiful.
That alone was a shock to Yamamoto, but when he heard what she said next, it set him thinking.
"It'll make a nice memory."

...A nice...memory...★
Yamamoto was deeply saddened that their days together were going to be turned into just a memory.
So he said it.
That they should meet again after camp was over.
That he wanted her to go out with him.
Then she blushed and said yes.
And she suggested they meet at the school gate at night, on the last day of camp.
He promised without a moment's hesitation.{p}

And then the last day of camp arrived.
That day he waited at the school gate, excited, planning to ask for her contact details and her class.
But she just wouldn't show up.
Yamamoto had been waiting since around seven.
Even at ten, she still hadn't come.
Yamamoto kept waiting anyway.
What if she'd come before seven?
And what if she'd gone home, thinking he wasn't coming...
Those thoughts crossed his mind too, but he kept on waiting.{p}

...She came.
At two in the morning.
She was wrapped in a black robe.
Her face was hidden by the robe.
So he couldn't see her face clearly.
The black robe gave off an air so dark it seemed about to melt into the night.
Yamamoto took hold of the robe, trying to see her face.
And then...{p}

"How nice of you to come waltzing right in."
A deep, gruff voice spoke, one that couldn't possibly be hers.
It was a voice that seemed to echo up from the depths of the earth.
"Now I'll kill you, just as the prophecy said..."
What had come to the school gate was the Reaper.
As for the real girl...{p}

She was apparently a girl who had died three years earlier.
She had run away from home in the very same season as Yamamoto's training camp, and stayed in the school's lodge all by herself.
And after spending day after day alone at the school, she must have grown dark and depressed.
Or perhaps the spirits that stir in this school were working on her.
She jumped from a window of the lodge...
After her suicide, her ghost would often appear in that lodge.
But now that Yamamoto has gone to the same world as her, I suppose she isn't lonely anymore.
Her ghost doesn't appear anymore.
Yamamoto, though, still seems to have lingering attachments to this world.
Ever since then, he's said to appear inside the lodge from time to time.
And after Yamamoto appears, her voice echoes all around...
And Yamamoto's ghost fades away in an instant, as if summoned by her voice, they say.
I couldn't do anything for Yamamoto.
That's why I quit the soccer club.
I was too afraid to face Yamamoto's ghost in the lodge...
That's the kind of man I am.
The lowest kind of man there is...
Well then, let me hand things over to the next person.
I've told you the truth.
So please, all of you, confess everything as well.
Now, whose turn is next...?{p}

I see.
Then I suppose I have no choice but to tell this story.
In that lodge... the Upside-Down Woman appears.
She's a monster who peers down at people sleeping in their beds.
Hanging head-down with her long hair dangling, she asks the person sleeping in the bed a certain question.
What kind of question, you ask?
That... I'll get to in due course.
It was last summer.
The soccer club I'd joined used that lodge for its training camps.
Actually, I joined the soccer club because a good friend of mine invited me.
Not that I had any thought of building up my body through sports or anything.
I just got interested from listening to my friend talk about it, that's all.{p}

That friend's name was Masaru Sodeyama.
The soccer club's training camp was brutally hard.
Sodeyama and I encouraged each other and endured the grueling practices.
And, well, during camp, Sodeyama ran into the Upside-Down Woman.
I hadn't even heard of the Upside-Down Woman myself until this incident happened.{p}

It was a hot, muggy night.
The lodge had no air conditioning and no window screens, so mosquitoes were flying all around in the heat; conditions couldn't have been worse.
And we had to lay our exhausted bodies down on those hard beds.
It was just miserable.
Even in the middle of the night, I couldn't get to sleep.
And then...{p}

The Upside-Down Woman appeared.
I was scared, so I pretended to be asleep.
From above Sodeyama's bed, the Upside-Down Woman stared down at him, as if peering into his face.
When Sodeyama sensed her presence and woke up, the Upside-Down Woman started saying this.
"So you woke up, did you?
Don't you tell anyone you met me.
This is a secret between just you and me.
You're a good boy, aren't you?{p}If you're a good boy, you can keep a promise, can't you?"
I won't tell anyone
Give no answer
Scream out loud
Shove her away

"Is that so?
You won't tell anyone, then.
That's a promise..."
With that, the Upside-Down Woman slid away, vanishing as if climbing upward.{p}

I had never heard such an eerie voice before.
Her voice was crushed and croaking, like a frog's.{p}

The next day, I followed him around everywhere.
I was worried he might break his promise to the Upside-Down Woman.
Sodeyama didn't tell anyone.
And so the day passed without incident, but...
Then came that night.{p}

The Upside-Down Woman appeared again.
And she said this.
"You didn't tell anyone, did you?
As a reward, I'll tell you something good.
Try telling someone you trust that you met me.
And try asking them what I really am..."
Having said only that, the Upside-Down Woman slid away and vanished once again.{p}

The next day, Sodeyama called me aside between practices and told me about the Upside-Down Woman.
I already knew the Upside-Down Woman had appeared to him.
So I was glad he came to me about it.
To him, I was someone he could trust.
That made me happy.
But that was when the tragedy happened.
The moment he finished telling me about the Upside-Down Woman...☆{p}

Blood sprayed everywhere.
The Upside-Down Woman's face and hands were drenched in blood.

Blood had gotten in my eyes, so I had no way of seeing what was happening.
But...
I do remember feeling something roll against my feet with a thud.
There was something attached to it, tangled and stringy like thread.{p}

Something like human hair.
And it crossed my mind.
Could this be...
Sodeyama's head...?
After that, I passed out.{p}

When I came to, I was lying in front of the incinerator.
I looked around and went to stand up, and...
In the flames of the incinerator, I saw something like a hand burning.
That must have been Sodeyama.
The Upside-Down Woman must have hacked him to pieces and thrown him into the incinerator.{p}

After that, I looked into the Upside-Down Woman.
The record was on the wall down low, beneath one of the beds in the lodge.
It must have been written long ago by someone who had run into the Upside-Down Woman.
A horrifying fact was written there.{p}

The Upside-Down Woman was a murderous monster.
First, she tries to make a promise with her prey.
The promise can be anything, but apparently it's usually to keep a secret.
And then, later, she comes to kill whoever breaks the promise.
It's a terrifying story.
There's no telling which bed in the lodge the Upside-Down Woman will appear at.
So you can't let your guard down.
When you're using that facility.
There's only one way to avoid being killed by the Upside-Down Woman.
You must never make a promise with her.
If you never make a promise, you can't break a promise to her, after all.
Or else, never break the promise.
But I think it's extremely hard to avoid breaking a promise to her.
She uses every trick there is to make her prey break the promise.
She doesn't kill anyone except those who've broken a promise.
She can't kill anyone else.
Why, you ask?
